title: Prospector logbook — Banyan Fintech outbound
content:
Context: Banyan Fintech (working name) — mid-market payments orchestration platform specializing in churn reduction for embedded finance partners. HQ NYC, ~220 employees, raised Series B 2022. Looking at product-led growth features for partners (white-label payflows + fraud signals). Heard from S. Kim (referral) that they are evaluating vendor partners for smarter routing of natural-language customer intents (support triage + auto refunds) and an offline reconciliation assistant for operations teams.

Objective: get a 30–45m discovery with Head of Platform (Anika Rao) + Ops lead (Tom Hsu). Goal: qualify for 6–8 week pilot (Dedicated capacity or Private pilot) to run 2 feature tests: (1) Intent classification + auto-reply for chargeback flows; (2) internal agent assistant for reconciliation and dispute summaries.

Key value props to lead with (tailored):
- Predictable latency for real-time chat triage (p95 < 120ms) vs incumbent serverless endpoints that spiked during holidays.
- Private deployment option (VPC) + KMS support — addresses data isolation ask from security team.
- Cost controls: batching + quantization guidance to keep per-token cost under their benchmark ($0.0008/token target).
- Rollout safety: automatic fallback to smaller model variants and canary policy for customer-facing routing.

Account research (quick hits):
- Tech signals: uses AWS (EKS, RDS Postgres), Kafka for event streams, uses Sentry + Datadog.
- Identity: Okta SSO; syncing customer meta via Segment.
- Public engineering hints: multiple PRs referencing Llama inference experiments in their public repo forks — suggests interest in fine-tuning and cost improvements.
- Security posture: SOC2 report public, but asked partners for ISO/PCI details in enterprise questionnaires.

Primary personas to map:
- Anika Rao, Head of Platform: cares about operational stability, latency SLAs, rollout controls, vendor lock-in.
- Tom Hsu, Ops Lead (payments ops): cares about accuracy of dispute summarization, audit trails, ability to replay inference results for compliance.
- Priya Malhotra, Security/Compliance: encryption, audit logs, data residency.
- Victor Li, Eng Manager (ML infra): cares about integration complexity, SDKs, inference formats, KV cache support, and ability to fine-tune/patch models.

Draft outbound sequence (email + call reminders):
- Day 0: Short intro email (see draft A), reference S. Kim intro, one-sentence value: reduce ops time on disputes by 30% and maintain same approval accuracy. Request 20-30m discovery.
- Day 3: Follow-up with one-pager + short technical call invite (10–15m).
- Day 10: Share an example playbook (chargeback intent classifier) + sample latency/cost estimates for a 50k monthly token workload.
- Day 18: LinkedIn touch and warm Slack DM (if contact via community).
- Day 30: Breakup email with offer of hosted sandbox access for a hands-on trial.

Email draft A (short, personalized):
Subject: Quick intro — reduce dispute review time at Banyan
Hi Anika —
S. Kim suggested I reach out — we help platform teams run LLM features with predictable latency and private deployment options. For payments ops teams we typically drive ~30% reduction in manual dispute review time by combining intent classification + an internal summarization assistant (keeps audit trail + deterministic fallback).
Would love 20 minutes to understand Banyan’s ops pain around chargebacks and share a short plan for a pilot. Open Wed/Thu morning next week?
Best,
Riya

Email draft B (technical, sent after intro):
Subject: pilot sketch — chargeback triage + reconciler (10–15m)
Anika —
Quick sketch: run a Dedicated instance (p95 < 120ms), deploy an intent classifier + summarizer. System outputs: (a) classification label + confidence, (b) short structured summary for Ops with links to source events, (c) signed audit record for compliance.
I can send a one-pager with cost/latency numbers if you’re open — 10–15m call to validate assumptions?
Riya

Call script bullets (discovery):
- Confirm base metrics: average disputes per week, SLA for response time, current human FTEs on dispute work, allowed false-positive rate.
- Ask about data access: event logs, refund policy rules, PII handling.
- Validate success criteria for pilot: latency target, % ops time reduction, auditability.
- Potential blockers: PCI scope expansion, SOC2 evidence needs, legal NDAs.

Objection handling (common):
- "We can't send data to third party": highlight Private deployment and VPC option + KMS + ability to run on-prem for pilot. Offer redacted-data sandbox for initial eval.
- "We already tried an LLM vendor; it was too inconsistent": talk about rollouts, automatic fallback to smaller models, and quality monitoring tied to prompt sets. Propose a short eval with our Optimize toolkit.
- "Cost seems unknown": provide cost modeling exercise: show batching/quantization levers and expected per-token range. Offer a 4-week cost review checkpoint.

Pilot sketch (6–8 weeks):
- Week 0: NDA + scoping call. Define datasets (anonymized dispute logs), acceptance criteria, and KPIs.
- Week 1–2: Fast integration — webhook + small ETL to push events to a sandbox, initial labeling sample (1–2k cases).
- Week 3–4: Model tuning/threshold calibration + latency tuning on Dedicated node. Run synthetic load and measure p95.
- Week 5: Ops shadow mode (no auto-actions) — report metrics, false-positive analysis.
- Week 6–7: Controlled rollout for a small subset (10% of flows) with auto-reply on low-risk labels.
- Week 8: Post-pilot review + pricing and next-steps (Dedicated reservation/Private licensing).

Metrics to track during pilot:
- Mean time to resolution for disputes (baseline vs pilot).
- p95 inference latency under real load.
- False positive rate for auto-replies.
- Tokens per session and monthly token estimate.
- Ops FTE hours saved (est.).

Integration checklist (tech):
- API keys + role-based access (Okta SSO mapping)
- Event webhook schema mapping (sample fields: event_id, user_id, transaction_id, timestamp, text_payload, metadata)
- Reconciliation output sink (S3 + signed audit record or internal DB insert)
- Logging and trace hooks for per-request observability (Datadog + request id)
- Replay tooling for compliance (ability to re-run inference on archived events)

Risks / open questions:
- PCI scope implications if chargebacks include card data in logs — need to confirm redaction before pilot.
- Legal: contract review for data processing agreement and subprocessor list.
- Engineering bandwidth: who owns the webhook + sample ETL? Suggested initial contacts: platform engineer (Victor), ops (Tom) — need explicit pairing.

Notes to self / next steps:
- Send draft A to Anika + cc S. Kim week of 11/13.
- Prep one-pager with p95 numbers and cost example for 50k monthly tokens (use Optimize defaults).
- Align with Solutions Eng (Miguel) to prepare sandbox image with VPC/Private sim and a short demo flow for ops.
- Pre-create a simple replay script and a small set of sample anonymized dispute records to show on call.

One-off message templates (short):
- Intro slack to engineering: "Hi Victor — Riya from Redwood. Would love 10m to confirm event schema for a quick sandbox integration. When's good?"
- Breakup: "Anika — closing the loop — if now isn't the right time I'd still be happy to share a sandbox you can spin up in an afternoon. Open to hand it off to your infra team. — Riya"

Tone and formatting guidance for collateral: keep one-pager < 1 page, bullets, include 3 explicit pilot acceptance criteria, include a single 90s demo GIF showing classification->summary->audit record.

Reflection: prioritize proving latency/SLA promise early in pilot — that is the main gating factor for Platform. Have Solutions Eng own a clear experiment that demonstrates p95 under holiday-like bursts (Kafka replay).

End of scratchpad.
